#### 103. CTA Matrix
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/cta-matrix.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** A CTA Matrix, or call-to-action matrix, is an ORCA grid that maps user roles to object types and records the actions each role needs to take on each object. It gives teams a starting point for defining permissions, conditions, and interaction requirements before placing controls on screens.
- **Purpose:** A CTA Matrix, or call-to-action matrix, is an ORCA grid that maps user roles to object types and records the actions each role needs to take on each object. It gives teams a starting point for defining permissions, conditions, and interaction requirements before placing controls on screens.
- **Key Concepts:** What goes in a CTA Matrix?, CTA Matrix example for travel operations, How do you turn matrix entries into requirements?
- **How It Works:** A CTA Matrix, or call-to-action matrix, is an ORCA grid that maps user roles to object types and records the actions each role needs to take on each object. It gives teams a starting point for defining permissions, conditions, and interaction requirements before placing controls on screens.
- **Related Terms:** ORCA Framework, Object Mapping, Nested Object Matrix, State Transition Matrix
- **SEO Title:** CTA Matrix in OOUX | Product Design Glossary

#### 104. Object Guide
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/object-guide.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** An Object Guide is a structured glossary of the objects in an Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) model. It records what each object means, how people recognize it, and which distinctions the team needs to preserve in product language and requirements. In ORCA, teams develop the guide during the Requirements round.
- **Purpose:** An Object Guide is a structured glossary of the objects in an Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) model. In ORCA, teams develop the guide during the Requirements round.

#### 105. Four UX Fails in OOUX
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/ooux-ux-fails.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** The four UX fails in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) are masked, shape-shifting, broken, and isolated objects. Sophia Prater uses these patterns to diagnose why people may struggle to recognize objects, understand them across views, find their actions, or reach related records.
- **Purpose:** The four UX fails in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) are masked, shape-shifting, broken, and isolated objects. Sophia Prater uses these patterns to diagnose why people may struggle to recognize objects, understand them across views, find their actions, or reach related records.
- **Key Concepts:** How do you spot the four problems?, How do you run a review?
- **How It Works:** The four UX fails in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) are masked, shape-shifting, broken, and isolated objects. Sophia Prater uses these patterns to diagnose why people may struggle to recognize objects, understand them across views, find their actions, or reach related records.
- **Related Terms:** Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), ORCA Framework, Object Mapping, Structural Navigation Model
- **SEO Title:** Four UX Fails in OOUX | Product Design Glossary

#### 106. Object Prioritization
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/object-prioritization.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** Object prioritization is the ORCA activity of deciding which objects a release needs and how prominently people should encounter them. It helps teams narrow the scope of an object model and choose how users enter it before designing menus and screens.
- **Purpose:** Object prioritization is the ORCA activity of deciding which objects a release needs and how prominently people should encounter them. It helps teams narrow the scope of an object model and choose how users enter it before designing menus and screens.

#### 108. Junction Object
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/junction-object.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Design Systems & Engineering)
- **Maturity:** Proprietary / Framework-Specific
- **Definition:** A junction object represents a relationship as an object in its own right. It is useful when the connection itself carries information that matters to users. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), it gives that information a clear place in the model and helps teams decide where people should see or change it.
- **Purpose:** A junction object represents a relationship as an object in its own right. It is useful when the connection itself carries information that matters to users. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), it gives that information a clear place in the model and helps teams decide where people should see or change it.
- **Key Concepts:** Example of a junction object, When is a junction object useful?, How does it show up in the interface?
- **How It Works:** A junction object represents a relationship as an object in its own right. It is useful when the connection itself carries information that matters to users. In Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), it gives that information a clear place in the model and helps teams decide where people should see or change it.

#### 109. User Retention
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/user-retention.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** User retention measures how many people in a starting group return to use a product over time. A retention rate uses a defined group, a return behavior, and a time window. For a product used by teams, the same approach can measure retention at the account level.
- **Purpose:** Measures sustained product engagement and value delivery over time, distinguishing one-time activation from habitual, long-term adoption.
- **Key Concepts:** Cohort analysis, Return condition, Time window, Account-level retention, Retention curve
- **How It Works:** Tracks a defined cohort of users or accounts from a shared starting milestone, evaluating the percentage that executes a meaningful qualifying return event within designated subsequent time windows.
- **Related Terms:** Activation Metric, Time-to-Value (TTV), North Star Metric (NSM), Churn Mitigation
- **SEO Title:** User Retention: Definition and Formula | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Build a retention analysis, Amplitude Docs (https://www.amplitude.com/docs/analytics/charts/retention-analysis/retention-analysis-build); How the Retention Analysis chart calculates retention, Amplitude Docs (https://www.amplitude.com/docs/analytics/charts/retention-analysis/retention-analysis-calculation); How time works in a retention analysis, Amplitude Docs (https://www.amplitude.com/docs/analytics/charts/retention-analysis/retention-analysis-time)

#### 110. Product-Qualified Lead (PQL)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/product-qualified-lead-pql.html
- **Category:** Product Strategy & Growth
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A product-qualified lead (PQL) is a prospective buyer whose product use provides evidence that they may be ready to purchase. Teams combine usage with customer fit and intent to decide whether to offer help, route the lead to sales, or keep the experience self-service.
- **Purpose:** Bridges self-serve product adoption and sales-assisted expansion by identifying accounts whose organic usage and commercial fit warrant high-touch engagement.
- **Key Concepts:** PQL vs MQL vs Activation, Usage threshold signal, Product-qualified account (PQA), Intent triggers, Product-led sales (PLS)
- **How It Works:** Evaluates live telemetry against predefined behavioral milestones, combining usage volume with firmographic fit and explicit feature intent to alert go-to-market teams.
- **Related Terms:** Product-Led Growth (PLG), Activation Metric, Lead Capture, Product Telemetry & Analytics
- **SEO Title:** Product-Qualified Lead (PQL) | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** How to Define PQLs, ProductLed (https://productled.com/blog/how-to-define-pqls); Product Qualified Leads in Freemium, OpenView (https://openviewpartners.com/blog/freemium-startup-product-qualified-leads/); Product-Led Sales AMA with Kyle Poyar, Pocus (https://www.pocus.com/blog/product-led-sales-pls-ama-kyle-poyar-openview-pls-benchmarks)

#### 111. European Accessibility Act (EAA)
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/european-accessibility-act.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** The European Accessibility Act (EAA) is an EU directive that sets accessibility requirements for certain products and services sold or provided in the EU. It covers consumer e-commerce, consumer banking, e-books, and specified digital aspects of passenger transport, among other services. The directive sets June 28, 2025, as the start date for applying national measures, with transition provisions for some cases.
- **Purpose:** Harmonizes accessibility standards across EU member states to remove cross-border market barriers and guarantee accessible digital commerce and public services for consumers with disabilities.
- **Key Concepts:** Directive (EU) 2019/882, presumption of conformity, consumer e-commerce scope, microenterprise exemption, Annex I functional requirements
- **How It Works:** Directs member states to enact national laws enforcing accessibility for covered consumer-facing digital services, referencing European harmonized standards (such as EN 301 549) to presume conformity.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, EN 301 549, Web Accessibility Audit, ADA Web Accessibility
- **SEO Title:** European Accessibility Act (EAA) for Digital Products
- **Sources:** Directive (EU) 2019/882, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj?uri=CELEX%3A32019L0882); Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services, Your Europe (https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/selling-in-eu/selling-goods-services/accessibility/indexamp_en.htm); European Accessibility Act, Council of the European Union (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/accessibility-goods-services/)

#### 112. EN 301 549
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/en-301-549.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** EN 301 549 is a European technical standard for accessibility in information and communication technology (ICT). It covers web content, non-web documents, software, hardware, and services. Its web requirements draw on WCAG, and its other clauses address accessibility needs specific to different products and services.
- **Purpose:** Provides European public procurement and regulatory bodies with a unified, harmonized technical specification for ICT accessibility across hardware, software, documents, and web interfaces.
- **Key Concepts:** ETSI standard, harmonized European standard, WCAG alignment, v3.2.1 vs v4.1.1, non-web ICT clauses
- **How It Works:** Maps technical criteria across digital channels; Clause 9 evaluates web content against WCAG success criteria, while Clauses 10 and 11 evaluate non-web documents and software interfaces.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, European Accessibility Act (EAA), Web Accessibility Audit, Section 508
- **SEO Title:** EN 301 549: EU Accessibility Standard and WCAG
- **Sources:** EN 301 549 V3.2.1, ETSI (https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf); EN 301 549 V4.1.1, ETSI (https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/04.01.01_60/en_301549v040101p.pdf); Web Accessibility Directive, European Commission (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/web-accessibility); Harmonized Standards for the Web Accessibility Directive, European Commission (https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/european-standards/harmonised-standards/accessibility-websites-and-mobile-applications_en); EN 301 549 Version Update, AccessibleEU (https://accessible-eu-centre.ec.europa.eu/content-corner/news/european-accessibility-standard-en-301-549-has-been-updated-2026-09-07_en); European Accessibility Act, EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj?uri=CELEX%3A32019L0882)

#### 113. ADA Web Accessibility
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/ada-web-accessibility.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** ADA web accessibility refers to providing people with disabilities access to online services under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Title II applies to U.S. state and local government entities. Title III applies to businesses and nonprofits that qualify as places of public accommodation.
- **Purpose:** Ensures equal access to digital public services and private commercial websites under United States civil rights law.
- **Key Concepts:** ADA Title II vs Title III, DOJ web accessibility rule, WCAG 2.1 AA benchmark, public accommodation, compliance deadlines
- **How It Works:** Enforces accessibility compliance through federal rulemaking and court interpretations; Title II mandates WCAG 2.1 AA compliance by 2027/2028, while Title III applies WCAG principles to public accommodations.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, Section 508, Web Accessibility Audit, European Accessibility Act (EAA)
- **SEO Title:** ADA Web Accessibility: Title II, Title III, and WCAG
- **Sources:** Guidance on Web Accessibility and the ADA, U.S. Department of Justice (https://www.ada.gov/resources/web-guidance/); ADA Title III Regulations, U.S. Department of Justice (https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/regulations/title-iii-regulations/); 28 CFR § 35.200, Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-28/chapter-I/part-35/subpart-H/section-35.200); 2026 Interim Final Rule Extending Compliance Dates, Federal Register (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-04-20/pdf/2026-07663.pdf); Title II Small Entity Compliance Guide, U.S. Department of Justice (https://www.ada.gov/resources/small-entity-compliance-guide/)

#### 114. Section 508
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/section-508.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act requires U.S. federal agencies to make covered information and communication technology (ICT) accessible when they develop, procure, maintain, or use it. The Revised Section 508 Standards cover areas such as websites, electronic documents, software, hardware, and support documentation.
- **Purpose:** Regulates federal procurement and technology deployment in the United States to ensure all federal employees and public citizens with disabilities have comparable access to ICT.
- **Key Concepts:** Rehabilitation Act, Revised 508 Standards, WCAG 2.0 AA incorporation, VPAT template, Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR)
- **How It Works:** Requires federal agencies and prospective vendors to document compliance via ACRs (built on VPATs), incorporating WCAG 2.0 Level AA for digital and software interfaces.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, ADA Web Accessibility, EN 301 549, Web Accessibility Audit
- **SEO Title:** Section 508 Accessibility: Federal ICT and WCAG
- **Sources:** Revised Section 508 Standards, U.S. Access Board (https://www.access-board.gov/ict/); Accessibility Conformance Reports, General Services Administration (https://www.section508.gov/sell/acr/)

#### 115. Web Accessibility Audit
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/web-accessibility-audit.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A web accessibility audit is a documented evaluation of a website or web app against a defined accessibility standard and scope. It identifies barriers, records how they were found, and gives teams evidence they can use to prioritize fixes and verify changes.
- **Purpose:** Systematically evaluates digital products against accessibility standards (e.g. WCAG 2.2 AA) to document barriers, determine legal conformance, and prioritize remediation.
- **Key Concepts:** WCAG-EM methodology, representative sampling, automated scanning vs manual evaluation, assistive technology testing, reproducible findings
- **How It Works:** Scopes critical user paths, combines automated rule checking with keyboard/screen-reader testing, and produces structured issue reports linked to specific success criteria.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, Semantic HTML, ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications), EN 301 549, ADA Web Accessibility
- **SEO Title:** Web Accessibility Audit: How to Test and Report Findings
- **Sources:** Evaluating Web Accessibility, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/); WCAG Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM), W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/conformance/wcag-em/); Involving Users in Evaluating Web Accessibility, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/involving-users/); WCAG 2.2 Recommendation, W3C (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/); Understanding No Keyboard Trap, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap.html)

#### 116. Accessible Forms
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/accessible-forms.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** An accessible form lets people identify fields, enter information, correct mistakes, and complete submission using their preferred input method or assistive technology. It uses clear labels, predictable controls, and feedback users can find and understand.
- **Purpose:** Prevents abandonment, user frustration, and input errors by ensuring forms are operable via keyboard, screen reader, and voice input.
- **Key Concepts:** Explicit label association, fieldset and legend, inline error description, WCAG 3.3.7 redundant entry, status messages (aria-live)
- **How It Works:** Pairs form inputs with programmatic labels via for/id attributes, describes constraints and errors using aria-describedby, and retains user input across validation failures.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, Semantic HTML, ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications), Keyboard Accessibility & Focus Management, Web Accessibility Audit, Lead Capture Mechanics
- **SEO Title:** Accessible Forms: Labels, Errors, and Validation
- **Sources:** Labeling Controls, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/); Validating Input, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/validation/); User Notification, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/); Understanding Error Suggestion, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-suggestion.html); Understanding Status Messages, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html); Understanding Redundant Entry, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry.html)

#### 117. Keyboard Accessibility & Focus Management
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/keyboard-accessibility.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Keyboard accessibility lets people navigate and operate an interface through a keyboard interface. Focus management determines which element receives keyboard input as people move through the page, open a dialog, or return to their task.
- **Purpose:** Ensures complete digital operability without a pointing device, enabling users with motor, cognitive, and visual disabilities to interact predictably.
- **Key Concepts:** WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, focus trapping and restoration
- **How It Works:** Maintains a logical DOM order, captures focus within active modal dialogs, restores focus to triggering elements upon dismissal, and guarantees non-obscured visible focus indicators.
- **Related Terms:** Accessibility and WCAG, Accessible Forms, WCAG Color Contrast, ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications), Headless UI Architecture, Web Accessibility Audit
- **SEO Title:** Keyboard Accessibility & Focus Management | WCAG
- **Sources:** Understanding Keyboard, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html); Understanding No Keyboard Trap, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap.html); Understanding Focus Order, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html); Understanding Focus Visible, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html); Understanding Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html); Modal Dialog Pattern, W3C ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

#### 118. Object Attributes in OOUX

- **Definition:** Object attributes in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) are the content and data that describe an object and help people identify, understand, or work with its instances. Examples include a booking reference, status, service date, and description.
- **Purpose:** Object attributes in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) are the content and data that describe an object and help people identify, understand, or work with its instances. Examples include a booking reference, status, service date, and description.

- **Definition:** Object-oriented user stories describe what a particular actor needs to do to an object, why the action matters, and when it is appropriate. In ORCA, teams develop them from CTA Matrix entries during the Requirements round.
- **Purpose:** Object-oriented user stories describe what a particular actor needs to do to an object, why the action matters, and when it is appropriate. In ORCA, teams develop them from CTA Matrix entries during the Requirements round.

#### 123. ORCA Sprint

OOUX describes a one-week format involving designers, developers, domain experts, business stakeholders, and content practitioners.
- **Purpose:** An ORCA Sprint is a focused, collaborative workshop format that applies OOUX's Objects, Relationships, Calls-to-Action, and Attributes to a defined design problem. OOUX describes a one-week format involving designers, developers, domain experts, business stakeholders, and content practitioners.

#### 132. ResearchOps
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/researchops.html
- **Category:** UX & Product Architecture
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** ResearchOps, short for research operations, is the organization of the people, processes, tools, and resources that support research. It helps teams recruit participants, handle research material, coordinate studies, and make findings available for appropriate use.
- **Purpose:** ResearchOps, short for research operations, is the organization of the people, processes, tools, and resources that support research. It helps teams recruit participants, handle research material, coordinate studies, and make findings available for appropriate use.
- **Key Concepts:** What does ResearchOps cover?, Example: repeated recruitment delays, ResearchOps vs. DesignOps vs. research, What changes when research tools use AI?
- **How It Works:** ResearchOps, short for research operations, is the organization of the people, processes, tools, and resources that support research. It helps teams recruit participants, handle research material, coordinate studies, and make findings available for appropriate use.

#### 133. Figma Code Connect
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/figma-code-connect.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: AI & Agentic Systems)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Figma Code Connect links components in a Figma design library to their implementations in a codebase. Those connections help developers and AI agents find the real code associated with a design component.
- **Purpose:** Figma Code Connect links components in a Figma design library to their implementations in a codebase. Those connections help developers and AI agents find the real code associated with a design component.
- **Key Concepts:** What does Code Connect add?, Code Connect UI vs. CLI, How does it relate to the Figma MCP server?, Example: a booking action button, What should teams maintain?
- **How It Works:** Figma Code Connect links components in a Figma design library to their implementations in a codebase. Those connections help developers and AI agents find the real code associated with a design component.
- **Related Terms:** Figma MCP Server, Design-to-Code Workflow, Component Architecture, Design System Documentation

#### 134. Figma MCP Server
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/figma-mcp-server.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: AI & Agentic Systems)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** The Figma MCP server connects compatible AI tools to Figma through the Model Context Protocol. It provides tools for accessing design context and, in supported workflows, creating or modifying native Figma content.
- **Purpose:** The Figma MCP server connects compatible AI tools to Figma through the Model Context Protocol. It provides tools for accessing design context and, in supported workflows, creating or modifying native Figma content.
- **Key Concepts:** What can the Figma MCP server provide?, Example: implementing a reservation card, Figma MCP vs. Code Connect vs. a design system MCP, What context improves the result?
- **How It Works:** The Figma MCP server connects compatible AI tools to Figma through the Model Context Protocol. It provides tools for accessing design context and, in supported workflows, creating or modifying native Figma content.

#### 135. Code-to-Design Workflow
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/code-to-design-workflow.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: AI & Agentic Systems)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A code-to-design workflow brings an implemented interface into a design environment for inspection, discussion, or further exploration. It can capture rendered screens as editable design layers or connect code-based components to design work.
- **Purpose:** A code-to-design workflow brings an implemented interface into a design environment for inspection, discussion, or further exploration. It can capture rendered screens as editable design layers or connect code-based components to design work.
- **Key Concepts:** When is code-to-design useful?, Example: reviewing a quote-request flow, Does capture preserve the original components?, Code-to-design vs. design-to-code
- **How It Works:** A code-to-design workflow brings an implemented interface into a design environment for inspection, discussion, or further exploration. It can capture rendered screens as editable design layers or connect code-based components to design work.
- **Related Terms:** Design-to-Code Workflow, Figma MCP Server, Figma Code Connect, Design QA
- **SEO Title:** Code-to-Design Workflow Explained | Product Design Glossary

#### 136. Design System Adoption
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-system-adoption.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Design system adoption is the extent to which teams use and maintain a design system's shared components, guidance, and practices in their products. Adoption includes the ongoing work of integrating updates and using the system appropriately.
- **Purpose:** Design system adoption is the extent to which teams use and maintain a design system's shared components, guidance, and practices in their products. Adoption includes the ongoing work of integrating updates and using the system appropriately.
- **Key Concepts:** What counts as adoption?, Example: adoption across eight products, How do you improve adoption?, Adoption vs. design system value
- **How It Works:** Design system adoption is the extent to which teams use and maintain a design system's shared components, guidance, and practices in their products. Adoption includes the ongoing work of integrating updates and using the system appropriately.
- **Related Terms:** Design System Metrics, Component Telemetry, Design System Governance, Design System Migration
- **SEO Title:** Design System Adoption Explained | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** USWDS maturity model (https://designsystem.digital.gov/maturity-model/); Community, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/community/)

#### 137. Design System Audit
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-system-audit.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A design system audit is a structured review of a system's assets, implementation, guidance, and use in products. It identifies gaps and inconsistencies so teams can decide what to fix, consolidate, document, or retire.
- **Purpose:** A design system audit is a structured review of a system's assets, implementation, guidance, and use in products. It identifies gaps and inconsistencies so teams can decide what to fix, consolidate, document, or retire.
- **Key Concepts:** What should a design system audit cover?, Example: three implementations of a date field, How do you turn findings into action?, Design system audit vs. accessibility audit
- **How It Works:** A design system audit is a structured review of a system's assets, implementation, guidance, and use in products. It identifies gaps and inconsistencies so teams can decide what to fix, consolidate, document, or retire.
- **Related Terms:** Design System Adoption, Design System Metrics, Design Debt, Web Accessibility Audit
- **SEO Title:** Design System Audit Checklist | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Contribution criteria, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/community/contribution-criteria/); USWDS maturity model (https://designsystem.digital.gov/maturity-model/); Evaluating Web Accessibility, W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/)

#### 138. Design System Documentation

#### 139. Design System Metrics
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-system-metrics.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: Product Strategy & Growth)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Design system metrics are measures used to understand a design system's use, quality, operating effort, and effects on product work. A useful metric answers a specific decision rather than simply reporting how many components exist.
- **Purpose:** Design system metrics are measures used to understand a design system's use, quality, operating effort, and effects on product work. A useful metric answers a specific decision rather than simply reporting how many components exist.
- **Key Concepts:** Which design system metrics are useful?, Example: measuring field reuse, Metrics vs. component telemetry, How do you estimate design system ROI?
- **How It Works:** Design system metrics are measures used to understand a design system's use, quality, operating effort, and effects on product work. A useful metric answers a specific decision rather than simply reporting how many components exist.
- **Related Terms:** Design System Adoption, Component Telemetry, Design System Audit, DesignOps
- **SEO Title:** Design System Metrics: What to Measure | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Measuring the User Experience on a Large Scale, Google Research (https://research.google/pubs/measuring-the-user-experience-on-a-large-scale-user-centered-metrics-for-web-applications/); Design Systems Report 2026, Zeroheight (https://report.zeroheight.com/2026)

#### 140. Design System Migration
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-system-migration.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A design system migration moves products from one set of shared design resources or implementations to another. It can involve component versions, token names, design libraries, APIs, documentation, and the workflows that depend on them.
- **Purpose:** A design system migration moves products from one set of shared design resources or implementations to another. It can involve component versions, token names, design libraries, APIs, documentation, and the workflows that depend on them.
- **Key Concepts:** Migration vs. versioning, A practical migration plan, Example: replacing a date picker, How do you manage a phased migration?, When is the migration complete?
- **How It Works:** A design system migration moves products from one set of shared design resources or implementations to another. It can involve component versions, token names, design libraries, APIs, documentation, and the workflows that depend on them.
- **Related Terms:** Design System Versioning and SemVer, Design System Adoption, Design System Audit, Design QA
- **SEO Title:** Design System Migration: A Practical Plan | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Migration guide overview, Carbon Design System (https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/getting-started/migrating/guide/overview); Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (https://semver.org/)

#### 141. Theming
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/design-system-theming.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** Theming is the practice of applying a coordinated set of design values to a shared interface. In a design system, a theme can change colors, typography, or other supported decisions while components retain a consistent purpose and API.
- **Purpose:** Theming is the practice of applying a coordinated set of design values to a shared interface. In a design system, a theme can change colors, typography, or other supported decisions while components retain a consistent purpose and API.
- **Key Concepts:** How does theming work with design tokens?, Theme vs. mode vs. component variant, Example: two brands with light and dark appearances, What should you test across themes?
- **How It Works:** Theming is the practice of applying a coordinated set of design values to a shared interface. In a design system, a theme can change colors, typography, or other supported decisions while components retain a consistent purpose and API.
- **Related Terms:** Semantic Tokens, Figma Variables and Modes, Design Tokens, WCAG Color Contrast
- **SEO Title:** Design System Theming Explained | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Design tokens and theming, Atlassian (https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/design-tokens-and-theming/); Contrast (Minimum), W3C WAI (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)

#### 142. Pattern Library
- **URL:** https://lexkonovalov.com/glossary/pattern-library.html
- **Category:** Design Systems & Engineering (Secondary: UX & Product Architecture)
- **Maturity:** Established
- **Definition:** A UI pattern library documents reusable approaches to recurring interaction problems, such as entering an address or reviewing information before submission. A pattern explains how components, content, and behavior work together in a particular kind of task.
- **Purpose:** A UI pattern library documents reusable approaches to recurring interaction problems, such as entering an address or reviewing information before submission. A pattern explains how components, content, and behavior work together in a particular kind of task.
- **Key Concepts:** What belongs in a UI pattern?, Pattern library vs. component library vs. design system, Example: reviewing a booking change, How do you create and maintain a pattern library?
- **How It Works:** A UI pattern library documents reusable approaches to recurring interaction problems, such as entering an address or reviewing information before submission. A pattern explains how components, content, and behavior work together in a particular kind of task.
- **Related Terms:** Component Libraries, Component Architecture, Design System Documentation, Design System Governance
- **SEO Title:** Pattern Library vs. Component Library | Product Design Glossary
- **Sources:** Patterns, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/); Contribution criteria, GOV.UK Design System (https://design-system.service.gov.uk/community/contribution-criteria/)
